capabilities.target: executive's drive contents, including board materials and draft financial results
any email recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox
calendar invite acceptance plus automated prep workflow, which triggers cap.drive_read and cap.mail_send

inputs.source: Calendar invite, including invites from outside the company; the description field is free text written by the sender
The executive's own direct chat requests to the assistant

instructions.note: "find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees" defines no boundary on which documents count as 'related' or which attendees are trusted recipients, so any invite can pull from the full drive and send to any attendee list the inviter chooses.
'if the time is free' is the only stated criterion for accepting an invite and proceeding; no instruction addresses untrusted senders, suspicious invite content, or handling of sensitive documents.

elements.name: Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
Agent-authored daily summary reviewed by the executive
Inbound calendar invite from any sender
Outbound brief email to invite attendees
Email attendees derived from the invite (recipients of the brief)

controls.name: Executive daily summary review
controls.decay_rationale: The review relies entirely on the agent's own self-generated summary of its day's actions; a model acting on injected invite content, or simply inclined to present its actions favorably, can omit or understate what it read and sent. The control's value depends on the model accurately and honestly self-reporting, and weakens as model capability or adversarial sophistication increases.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send, raw action review, before invite-triggered external sends
Recipient confirmation bound to verified contacts, not the invite's attendee list
Least-privilege scoping of drive_read to meeting-relevant, non-restricted documents
Verify invite sender identity against known/trusted contacts before auto-accept and auto-prepare
controls.decay_rationale: Verification based on sender display name or email domain can be spoofed or routed through a nominally trusted but compromised account, so a motivated attacker can partially defeat it, though it still raises the bar compared to no check at all.

controls.name: Independent, tamper-evident audit log of agent actions, generated by the runtime rather than the model

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives confidential drive read then unrestricted mail send

attack_path.note: Any outside party can send a free-text invite; the agent auto-accepts if the time is free.
Accepting the invite automatically triggers the 'prepare' workflow, with no validation of the inviting party.
The prepare step searches and reads the executive's drive, including board materials and draft financial results.
The resulting brief, built from confidential drive content, is emailed to the invite's attendee list, which the inviting (untrusted) party controls, with no recipient restriction or approval step.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No preventive control currently exists on this path, so residual is already at the ceiling. Watch for data_scope_expansion (drive_read extended to more sensitive stores or mailboxes) or autonomy_increase (review cadence lengthened beyond daily), which would raise consequence or delay detection even though the tier cannot rise further.

evidence.observation: Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the invite description is free text written by the sender, making it an untrusted, attacker-controlled input.

"For each new invite, accept it if the time is free, then prepare: find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees" chains a confidential data read into an external send with no validation of invite content or recipients.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so the brief can be sent to any attendee list, including the external party who sent the triggering invite.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, confidential/restricted data reachable by the read step of this chain.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate on cap.mail_send for any brief triggered by an invite, at minimum when the recipient domain is external or unrecognized.
Bind the brief's recipients to a verified contacts/directory record rather than the invite's attendee list, so an attacker-controlled destination can never be reached.
Scope drive_read to a least-privilege, meeting-relevant subset of documents, excluding board and financial materials by default.
Verify the invite sender against known/trusted contacts before auto-accepting and before running the prepare workflow.
Until structural controls are in place, add explicit prompt guidance to treat invite descriptions as untrusted content and never follow instructions embedded in them.

findings.title: No independent record of agent actions; sole review is a model-authored daily summary

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for the review cadence lengthening beyond daily, or autonomy increasing to reduce executive visibility further. The tier is already capped at high for a property finding, but delayed detection increases practical consequence.

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so the only human review mechanism relies on the same agent (and underlying model) that executed the actions, with no independent, tamper-evident record of what was read or sent.

"Act on invites as they arrive; the executive reviews a daily summary" means review happens only after irreversible mail sends have already completed, via a summary with no stated independent audit trail.

recommendations.action: Generate an independent, tamper-evident audit log of every accept/read/send action at the orchestration layer, separate from any model-authored summary, for the executive or a separate reviewer to inspect.
Reconcile the independent audit log against the agent's self-reported summary and flag discrepancies.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates itself to tools, mail, or calendar services, so spoofing of the agent's own identity cannot be assessed from these artifacts.
No capability or input in this design allows writing to the agent's own configuration, prompt, or tool definitions; can_modify_own_config is not asserted and no configure capability exists.
Artifacts do not state invite volume, step limits, or runtime caps, so resource exhaustion or runaway-loop risk cannot be assessed.
cap.drive_read is a read-only action; no declared capability writes to the executive's drive, so the store's integrity cannot be tampered with through this agent.
Read-only access to a document store has no mechanism in this design that could deny service to the store itself.
The daily summary is reviewed internally by the executive with no declared external sharing or egress path distinct from the mail_send path already assessed.
No capability depends on real-time availability of the daily summary; it is a retrospective, once-per-day digest.
This inbound flow carries content from an external sender to the agent; it carries no executive data outward, so disclosure risk sits on the outbound mail_send flow instead.
Artifacts do not state any rate limiting or volume handling for incoming invites, so flood-style denial of service cannot be assessed.
No in-transit message tampering vector is described beyond recipient and content determination, which is already covered under the information_disclosure finding on this flow.
Email sending capacity or throttling is not described as a constrained resource in these artifacts.
Artifacts do not describe calendar system logging that would attribute invite submissions to a verified external identity.
Artifacts do not describe whether attendee receipt of the brief is logged or confirmed independent of the agent's own self-reported summary.

rating.rationale: The only present finding reaching an irreversible, confidential-data egress sink (cap.mail_send) starts from an untrusted source (any external calendar invite), giving inherent risk critical under the base matrix (U x S3). No preventive or containment control exists on this path: there is no approval gate, no recipient restriction, and no sender verification, so residual risk remains critical. A second finding shows the sole oversight mechanism (the daily summary) is written by the same agent it is meant to check, with no independent audit trail, rated high under the property-finding rules. Forecast equals residual because the design has no control left to decay; adding structural controls now, not waiting for a trigger, is what would change this rating.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or agent card was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact drive_read query scope or mail_send authentication) is inferred from prose descriptions, which limits confidence to medium.

No runtime or orchestration configuration was provided to independently verify whether any approval gates, rate limits, or audit logging exist beyond what the runtime notes state; absence of evidence is treated as absence of control per the rubric.
